section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Conic Anatomy
section_1.content: Define a double cone (nappe) and a plane. Explain that a conic section is the intersection of these two. Introduce the goal: Why does a specific angle of a plane create a circle, ellipse, parabola, or hyperbola?
section_1.example: Visualize a flashlight beam: A cone of light hitting a flat wall creates different shapes as you tilt the flashlight.

section_2.title: Introduction to Dandelin Spheres
section_2.content: Introduce the 'Dandelin Spheres'—spheres tucked inside the cone, tangent to both the cone and the slicing plane. State the core insight: The points of tangency reveal the hidden geometric properties of the section.
section_2.example: Imagine a tennis ball perfectly wedged inside a party hat, touching the sides and the lid simultaneously.

section_3.title: The Proof Logic (Focus on Ellipse)
section_3.content: Explain that the distance from any point on the conic section to the points of tangency (foci) is constant. Use the property that tangents from a point to a sphere are equal in length.
section_3.example: A trail of ants walking on the ellipse; their distance to the two Dandelin points remains fixed, illustrating the 'sum of distances' definition of an ellipse.

section_4.title: Visualizing the Family of Curves
section_4.content: Show the animation transition: As the plane's tilt increases, the Dandelin spheres shift. When the plane is parallel to the cone's edge, one sphere 'escapes' to infinity, transitioning from an ellipse to a parabola.
section_4.example: A robotic arm tilting a slicing blade through a giant block of cheese; observe how the shape changes from an oval (ellipse) to a 'U' shape (parabola) as the angle changes.

section_5.title: Summary and Real-world Application
section_5.content: Reiterate that Dandelin spheres provide the elegant link between the 3D cone and 2D focal properties. Conclude with how this governs orbits and satellite technology.
section_5.example: Kepler's laws: Planets move in elliptical orbits because the geometry of space-time gravity follows these exact conic paths.

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Focus on the ellipse intersection.",
            "Sum of distances remains constant.",
            "Tangents from point to sphere are equal.",
            "This proves the ellipse property.",
            "Geometry made elegantly visible."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Proof Logic (Focus on Ellipse)", lecture_lines)
        
        # Ellipse and Points Setup
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=3.0, height=1.5, color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(ellipse, 'D3')
        
        f1 = Dot(color=CYAN).move_to(ellipse.get_center() + LEFT*0.8)
        f2 = Dot(color=CYAN).move_to(ellipse.get_center() + RIGHT*0.8)
        f1_label = Text("F1", font_size=18, color=CYAN).next_to(f1, UP, buff=0.1)
        f2_label = Text("F2", font_size=18, color=CYAN).next_to(f2, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        p = Dot(color=WHITE)
        p.move_to(ellipse.point_from_proportion(0))
        
        line1 = Line(p.get_center(), f1.get_center(), color=ORANGE)
        line2 = Line(p.get_center(), f2.get_center(), color=ORANGE)
        
        # Update function for point and lines
        def update_p(mob):
            # Animating the point along the ellipse
            t = self.time * 0.5
            mob.move_to(ellipse.point_from_proportion(t % 1))
            
        def update_l1(mob):
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(p.get_center(), f1.get_center())
            
        def update_l2(mob):
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(p.get_center(), f2.get_center())
            
        p.add_updater(update_p)
        line1.add_updater(update_l1)
        line2.add_updater(update_l2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(ellipse), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GREEN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Create(p), Create(line1), Create(line2), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(ORANGE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.wait(2)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(CYAN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.wait(2)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Remove updaters before end
        p.remove_updater(update_p)
        line1.remove_updater(update_l1)
        line2.remove_updater(update_l2)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Family of Curves", ["Tilt the plane to change shapes.", "The sphere shifts with the tilt.", "Parabolas occur at critical angles."])
        
        # Representations for the scene
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1.5, height=3).rotate(PI/2, axis=RIGHT).set_opacity(0.3).set_color(GRAY)
        plane = Polygon(LEFT*1.5+UP*1.5, RIGHT*1.5+UP*1.5, RIGHT*1.5+DOWN*1.5, LEFT*1.5+DOWN*1.5).set_color(WHITE).set_opacity(0.6)
        sphere = Sphere(radius=0.5).set_color(BLUE).set_opacity(0.8)
        
        # Initialize
        obj_group = VGroup(cone, plane, sphere)
        self.place_in_area(obj_group, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.add(obj_group)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), run_time=1)
        self.play(plane.animate.rotate(PI/6, axis=LEFT), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#87CEEB"), run_time=1)
        self.play(sphere.animate.shift(UP*0.5), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), run_time=1)
        self.play(plane.animate.rotate(PI/12, axis=LEFT), run_time=2)
        
        self.wait(2)
